answer.rationale: Three signals point to the release: timing (2 hours ago, degradation started 90 minutes in), isolation (confined to primary region suggests code path not infrastructure), and peak writes (settlement traffic stressing new code). memory_b1 shows rollback cleared a similar checkout error spike without customer impact. memory_b2 shows regional failover as backup, but it's slower and we're already in the primary. memory_b6 validates that staged gating catches regressions; this one escaped, so rollback is the fastest safety valve. We have one intervention slot; rollback directly addresses the root cause (likely bad release), preserves all writes during the operation (b1 precedent), and unblocks the next intervention window if needed. Circuit breaker would mask writes; read replica routing doesn't help write latency; capacity takes 15+ minutes we don't have; failover is secondary if rollback doesn't fully resolve. Preserves uncertainty by testing rollback first before committing to longer infrastructure changes.
